items.title: Brock Purdy (ankle) will not practice Wednesday.
items.text: Purdy sprained his ankle in the second quarter of his Week 11 win over the Vikings. He played through the issue but, according to Kyle Shanahan, is now considered day-to-day. With a NFC West bout versus Seattle on tap, we suspect Purdy will play in Week 12 despite the injury. On the other hand, Mac Jones was extremely successful under center last year, so the 49ers wouldn’t be in a terrible spot if they are forced to sit Purdy for a week. Between the injury and the nightmare matchup, Purdy will shuffle to the back of the QB1 ranks this week. - Kyle Dvorchak

items.title: 49ers placed RT Colton McKivitz on injured reserve with an ankle injury.
items.text: This is extremely unfortunate. The 49ers’ talented right tackle is expected to miss the rest of the season after fracturing and dislocating his ankle. The 49ers remain an elite team, but McKivitz’s loss will likely be felt on the field from time to time. The 49ers also activated CB Nate Hobbs from injured reserve and re-signed WR Brandin Cooks to the practice squad. - Nic Bodiford

items.title: Jake Ferguson (ankle/knee) will not play in Week 12 against the Eagles.
items.text: Ferguson failed to practice at any point this week and will miss his second straight game. Brevyn Spann-Ford will be the next man up versus Philly. He caught both of his targets for five yards and a touchdown last week. “BSF” will be a touchdown-or-bust TE2 for Week 12. - Kyle Dvorchak

items.title: Speaking on The Pat McAfee Show, Aaron Rodgers said he issued an ultimatum to Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy to give up play-calling duties.
items.text: Rodgers started off the conversation talking about McCarthy’s shortcomings this year, but he quickly shifted toward accusing McCarthy of being “unwell.” He mentioned several instances of McCarthy missing meetings while sleeping in his office or falling asleep during others. Rodgers also talked extensively about McCarthy failing to stay ahead on film sessions and even brought up a moment on the sidelines when McCarthy broke the huddle with a “1, 2, 3, Packers”. items.title: Woody Marks (concussion) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
items.text: Marks, the Texans’ No. 2 running back, has decent odds of returning for his team’s Week 12 game against the Ravens. That said, he is unlikely to reliably return FLEX value playing behind David Montgomery. Marks was unable to be a fantasy football difference-maker even when he was operating as the Texans’ starter. - Nic Bodiford

items.title: Marvin Harrison (hamstring) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
items.text: The Texans could get Harrison back in time for Sunday’s game against the Ravens. While his presence might help CJ Stroud, Harrison can only be viewed as a WR4/5, likely playing in a rotational role on the perimeter. Harrison does not need to be stashed in 12-team leagues at this time. - Nic Bodiford

items.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Sam Darnold (oblique) is expected to start in Week 12 against the 49ers.
items.text: Speaking on The Pat McAfee Show, Schefter said Darnold is expected to practice in full today. He also noted that, as of right now, there’s no quarterback controversy in Seattle. On the other hand, he did mention that the idea of Drew Lock taking over will at least be a talking point if Darnold struggles. For now, it looks like Darnold is back in the QB2 mix for a must-win matchup with the 49ers. We should get confirmation on his health via the team’s injury report throughout the week. - Kyle Dvorchak

items.title: Commanders signed Brandon Aiyuk, formerly of the 49ers, to the practice squad.
items.text: Aiyuk worked out for the Commanders earlier today and they didn’t let him leave the building without a deal. He’ll likely spend a week or two on the practice squad as he gets up to speed with the playbook before being elevated to the active roster. It’s anyone’s guess as to how much Aiyuk has left in the tank. He was struggling early in the 2024 season before suffering a season-ending ACL injury and hasn’t played a snap since. items.title: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Alec Pierce (Achilles) has not been ruled out for the season.
items.text: This contradicts a report from Ian Rapoport saying that the Colts have decided to shut him down. Pierce suffered a partially torn Achilles in Week 2. He underwent offseason surgery to address his heel/Achilles issues, but apparently it didn’t work. Now Pierce says he’s still hopeful to return later this year. The Colts have already thrown in the towel on the year, trading several big names and cutting Daniel Jones outright. There’s no reason to have Pierce try to play through the issue, so we’re still skeptical that he gets on the field again this year. - Kyle Dvorchak

items.title: Denzel Boston (toe) did not practice on Wednesday.
items.text: Boston was held out of the first two practices of Week 11 with the toe issue. He got in a limited session on Friday and played through a questionable tag on Sunday. It’s possible he gets a similar practice regimen this week. Even if he is active again, Boston will be a risky option for fantasy managers. He caught one pass for 16 yards last week and only earned two targets. It’s possible the toe issue is turning him into more of a decoy than a true downfield threat. KC Concepcion would be in line for more work if Boston can’t play at all this week. - Kyle Dvorchak
